focus_area_title: Identify the Biases in Your Hiring Process
content_text_body:
There are multiple ways to tackle the unconscious biases we adopt. To start, it is essential we recognize how stereotypes guide an exclusionist perspective and harm progress toward hiring people from different backgrounds.   

### Slow down
Take the time to review your hiring process and identify patterns that might hinder your diversity goals. Reflect on your recruitment and hiring decisions to recognize tendencies that limit opportunities for talented candidates to adequately demonstrate their competence.  

### Who is in your pool of candidates? 
Examine your talent pool and determine if your outreach efforts are aligned with your diversity goals. Keep in mind diversity is not just about gender and race, instead diversity encompasses many other factors such as values, age, sexual orientation, and disabilities. 

### Your hiring must have an objective
Think about the type of person you want to bring into your team. Define clear candidate qualifications and structure your interviews to measure those qualifications in a realistic and practical way. For example, asking candidates to complete skills-based tasks reflecting every day duties will help you increase the effectiveness of your assessment process.   

Read more about how to [identify and reduce your bias in hiring](https://www.shrm.org/resourcesandtools/hr-topics/talent-acquisition/pages/7-practical-ways-to-reduce-bias-in-your-hiring-process.aspx) and use this guide to [recognize stereotyping patterns](https://biasinterrupters.org/wp-content/uploads/Identifying-Bias-in-Hiring-Worksheet.pdf).
